package_info.package_versions: Orion Platform versions released between March 2020 and June 2020 (exact versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2 with HF 1 and HF 2)
package_info.why_malicious: Malicious code was covertly injected into the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll during the official build process, resulting in a digitally signed, trojanized update. This update delivered the SUNBURST/Solorigate backdoor to customer environments, enabling persistent, stealthy remote access and command execution by attackers across thousands of organizations, including government and security industry targets.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (DLL load during Orion service startup)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Implements a covert backdoor that, upon loading the DLL, checks for network connectivity and anti-analysis conditions (such as debugger and sandbox detection), then beacons to a remote command-and-control server. If a command is received from the attacker, it executes arbitrary attacker-supplied instructions on the victim system, enabling remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code introduces hidden network communications and remote command execution capabilities into a core business logic DLL, which is not expected in legitimate SolarWinds Orion software. The presence of anti-debugging and anti-sandbox checks further indicates deliberate evasion of security analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business logic DLLs should not contain code for remote command-and-control, anti-analysis techniques, or arbitrary command execution. Such functionality is outside the scope of normal Orion operations and represents a severe violation of software integrity.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: While remote management tools may communicate with central servers, this is not expected from core business logic DLLs, especially not with embedded anti-analysis logic and covert command execution. Legitimate remote management is typically implemented in dedicated, auditable components, not hidden within trusted DLLs.
key_indicators: Presence of anti-debugging and anti-sandbox logic within the DLL
Remote command execution logic embedded in a core business logic component
Malicious code inserted into a digitally signed, trusted DLL
Execution of attacker-supplied instructions upon receiving C2 commands

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the SolarWinds build infrastructure and injects malicious code into the Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll source code or build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is compiled and digitally signed as part of the official SolarWinds Orion release, making it appear legitimate.

attack_chain.action: The trojanized DLL is distributed to customers through official SolarWinds update channels as part of routine software updates.
attack_chain.leads_to: Customers install the malicious update, resulting in the compromised DLL being loaded into their production environments.

attack_chain.action: When the Orion service starts, the malicious DLL is loaded and the backdoor logic executes automatically.
attack_chain.leads_to: The backdoor beacons to attacker-controlled infrastructure, establishing covert communication and awaiting further instructions.

attack_chain.action: The attacker issues commands to compromised systems via the backdoor, enabling lateral movement, data exfiltration, or further compromise within the victim environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker achieves persistent, covert control over victim environments, with the ability to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network communications initiated by SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll or Orion platform processes
Presence of anti-debugging or anti-sandbox logic within core Orion DLLs
Remote command execution capabilities detected in non-administrative or business logic components
Digitally signed SolarWinds binaries exhibiting command-and-control (C2) beaconing behavior
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (file hashes matching known trojanized versions)
Unexpected modifications or unauthorized changes to core Orion DLLs
DLLs with anomalous file size or compile timestamps inconsistent with official releases
network_indicators: Connections to known SUNBURST/Solorigate C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud[.]com)
Unusual outbound traffic from Orion servers to external IP addresses or domains not associated with SolarWinds operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity originating from Orion platform processes, especially connections to known malicious C2 domains such as avsvmcloud[.]com. Compare file hashes and compile timestamps of core DLLs against trusted baselines to identify unauthorized modifications. Analyze DLLs for embedded anti-analysis logic and remote command execution code. Alert on any digitally signed SolarWinds DLLs exhibiting beaconing or C2 behavior, and investigate any anomalous outbound connections from Orion servers.
